proposals.title: Monorepo scaffold, TypeScript strict config, and blocking lint gates
proposals.why_now: The repository contains zero source code after eight benchmark cycles. Every other proposal depends on a buildable workspace with enforced constraints. ADR-003, ADR-004, and Section 13 require compile-time and lint-time enforcement of determinism and dependency boundaries before any domain code is written — violations accumulate silently without these gates. FASE-1 acceptance criteria explicitly require lint of determinism and lint of dependency boundaries to be active and blocking in CI before acceptance.

acceptance_targets: docs/decisions/ADR-002-hash.md specifies the hash function bit-by-bit (e.g. SplitMix64 over FNV-1a accumulator of UTF-8 encoded arguments) with test vectors and the rationale for why it is not a native language hash

docs/decisions/ADR-009-encoder.md specifies CanonicalEncoder fully: UTF-8 byte-order key sorting applied recursively; bigint as signed decimal ASCII with explicit sign, no leading zeros, no exponential notation; safe integer with a distinct type marker so 1n and 1 never collide; prohibition of undefined, NaN, Infinity, -0 (occurrence is a thrown error); ordered vs unordered collection encodings; encodingVersion participation in the hash

docs/decisions/ADR-004-rounding.md specifies how rounding mode declaration is enforced at compile time or lint level — e.g. a divBigInt(a, b, mode) helper where the bare / operator on branded types is a lint error; the three modes TRUNCATE_TOWARD_ZERO, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_HALF_EVEN are typed constants

proposals.title: ADRs for hash function, CanonicalEncoder, and rounding-mode enforcement
proposals.why_now: Three DEFINIR items are prerequisites for all FASE-1 implementation and must be resolved in ADRs before any code that depends on them is written. ADR-009 explicitly states the CanonicalEncoder must be specified in a dedicated ADR before any state hash exists. ADR-002 states the hash function must be specified bit-by-bit in a dedicated ADR before the RNG is implemented. ADR-004 requires the technical enforcement mechanism for declaring rounding modes to be specified before any division operation is coded. Writing code before these ADRs is a spec violation that embeds decisions in code with no recorded rationale.

proposals.title: packages/core — branded numeric types, positional RNG, CanonicalEncoder, and packages/contracts
proposals.why_now: packages/core is the dependency of every other pure package. Without branded numeric types the type system cannot enforce ADR-003 or ADR-004. Without the positional RNG the price generator cannot be written. Without CanonicalEncoder no state hash can be computed. packages/contracts is required by FASE-1 acceptance because the simulation worker must have a typed IPC contract from the first commit. Everything else in FASE-1 depends on both packages existing and correct.

proposals.title: packages/world price generator, packages/domain ledger and market orders, packages/application tick loop
proposals.why_now: This is the functional core of FASE-1. The acceptance criteria require a price generator with two noise layers and two assets, a multi-commodity double-entry ledger, spot market buy and sell orders, and the canonical tick loop with ten steps in locked order. These three packages compose the minimum simulation required for INV-01 through INV-07, INV-13, INV-21, and INV-22 to become green tests. They arrive together because application composes world and domain without coupling them — implementing any one in isolation cannot be verified against the invariants. The price generator requires fixed-point or lookup-table implementations for log and exp (prohibited as floating-point) as specified in its own ADR.

proposals.title: Electron app scaffold, tools/replay, tools/bench, and full CI gate with installers
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires simulation running in a dedicated worker with typed IPC contract, a minimal installer for Windows and Linux produced by CI, tools/replay reporting the first divergent tick between two executions, and tools/bench with frozen calibration ratios. The spec warns that discovering packaging and ABI issues late is fatal — a minimal installer in FASE-1 is worth more than a polished one at FASE-7. INV-19 requires the CI matrix to compare worker simulation against tools/replay on both Windows and Linux. This proposal also delivers the minimal UI (chart, balance, buy/sell buttons, pause/1x) and the permanent disclaimer required by Section 20.

repository_assessment.current_state: Repository contains only git infrastructure, a frozen spec copy under benchmark/, benchmark history directories, and a README. No source code, no packages, no TypeScript configuration, no CI pipeline, no lint gates, no ADRs, no Electron scaffold, and no tooling exist anywhere in the workspace. Eight Ideator cycles have run; zero accepted changes have been committed. Every FASE-1 acceptance criterion remains entirely unmet.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The monorepo does not exist. There is no package structure, no TypeScript project, and no lint infrastructure. Without these, no code can be written in conformance with the spec's structural and determinism requirements. All subsequent FASE-1 work is blocked on this foundation being established first.

warnings: ADR-009 explicitly requires the CanonicalEncoder to be specified in a dedicated ADR before any state hash exists. ADR-002 requires the hash function to be specified bit-exactly in a dedicated ADR before the RNG is implemented. ADR-004 requires the rounding-mode enforcement mechanism to be specified in a dedicated ADR before any division operation is coded. IDEA-002 must be completed before any implementation in IDEA-003 begins, or the resulting code will embed unrecorded decisions that are a spec violation.

The price generator in §5.1 constructs prices in log-space, which requires log and exp. Both Math.log and Math.exp are prohibited in pure packages by §13. Fixed-point or lookup-table implementations that are bit-identical across IEEE-754 platforms must be specified in their own ADR before packages/world work begins; otherwise the price generator cannot be implemented without violating either §13 or the cross-platform determinism requirement of INV-19.

Section 14.3 notes that better-sqlite3 requires native recompilation for the Electron ABI and recommends deferring the SQLite driver choice to FASE-4. No SQLite dependency should be introduced in FASE-1; it would create a packaging and ABI problem before the team has established the build pipeline.

The number of octaves, their periods, and their amplitudes for trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise are DEFINIR (§5.1). These parameters must be recorded in a versioned config file and fixed before the price generator is implemented, because any change after the FASE-1 performance baseline is frozen requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates all reference StateHashes.
